toolTip.v:
BASIC is suitable for a beginner. Many parameters
are hidden from the user in this mode.
ADVANCED mode will make available all parameters.

To change the application LEVEL, go to:
Edit -> Preferences -> General and check:
'APP. LEVEL' radio button.

This selects the kind of geometries on the canvas to plot.
Those can be either of type 'Travel' which means the moves
above the work piece or it can be of type 'Cut',
which means the moves that cut into the material.
Start the Object Editor
Show the Properties.

This selects if to display text annotation on the plot.
When checked it will display numbers in order for each end
of a travel line.

This is the total travelled distance on X-Y plane.
In current units.

This is the estimated time to do the routing/drilling,
without the time spent in ToolChange events.

Tools in this CNCJob object used for cutting.
The tool diameter is used for plotting on canvas.
The 'Offset' entry will set an offset for the cut.
'Offset' can be inside, outside, on path (none) and custom.
'Type' entry is only informative and it allow to know the 
intent of using the current tool. 
It can be Rough(ing), Finish(ing) or Iso(lation).
The 'Tool type'(TT) can be circular with 1 to 4 teeths(C1..C4),
ball(B), or V-Shaped(V).
Plot (show) this object.
Update the plot.

When selected, it will include CNC Code snippets (append and prepend)
defined in the Preferences.
Enable the autolevelling feature.
Generate GCode that will obtain the height map
Toggle the display of the Probe Points table.

Plot the probing points in the table.
If a Voronoi method is used then
the Voronoi areas are also plotted.

Will create a GCode which will be sent to the controller,
either through a file or directly, with the intent to get the height map
that is to modify the original GCode to level the cutting height.
The safe Z for probe travelling between probe points.

The maximum depth that the probe is allowed
to probe. Negative value, in current units.
The feedrate used while the probe is probing.

Choose a mode for height map generation.
- Manual: will pick a selection of probe points by clicking on canvas
- Grid: will automatically generate a grid of probe points

Choose a method for approximation of heights from autolevelling data.
- Voronoi: will generate a Voronoi diagram
- Bilinear: will use bilinear interpolation. Usable only for grid mode.
The number of grid columns.
The number of grid rows.

The kind of controller for which to generate
height map gcode.
Lists the available serial ports.
Search for the available serial ports.
Lists the available serial ports.
New, custom baudrate.
Add the specified custom baudrate to the list.
Software reset of the controller.
Connect to the selected port with the selected baud rate.
Jog the Y axis.

Zero the CNC X axes at current position.
Zero the CNC Y axes at current position.
Zero the CNC Z axes at current position.
Perform a homing cycle on all axis.

Feedrate when jogging.

Print in shell the GRBL report.

Will send the probing GCode to the GRBL controller,
wait for the Z probing data and then apply this data
over the original GCode therefore doing autolevelling.
Will save the GRBL height map.
Will save the probing GCode.
View/Edit the probing GCode.

Import the file that has the Z heights

over the original GCode therefore
doing autolevelling.

Export and save G-Code to
